title: Compassion Benchmark Daily Briefing — October 22, 2026 (Paris and UNC Meet Their First Real Evidence)
headline: Paris's first measured score is 40.6; its published 62.5 is unchanged.
summary:
Nothing in this briefing has been applied. Every score named as published is the live score. Every other number is a proposal or a measurement.

Fifteen organizations were assessed. Three proposals were filed, all at low confidence: Paris, Portugal and the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC).

Paris and UNC had never been checked against evidence. Their published 62.5 and 43.8 were starting values. A first assessment measures Paris at 40.6 and UNC at 28.1. Most first assessments so far have come in below their starting value, so these are not measured declines in conduct.

The value given to missing evidence matters. Scored at 3 instead of 2 out of 5, UNC would read 41.3, which stays in the Functional band (40 to 60). Paris would read 50.0, also Functional.

Portugal measures 59.4 against a published 60.6, just below the Established line at 60, after police cleared housing camps on 20 October 2026. France measured 52.5 and Netflix 58.1. Neither was filed, because no court or watchdog source backs a band crossing.

Lisbon, Valencia and Spain matched proposals already on file. Seven other readings held.

Search quality was degraded. Three batches failed twice, and the search tool ignores OR and AND, so no result means not surfaced.

Release watch: 0 sources registered — detection did not run.

topSignals.title: Paris's 62.5 Was a Starting Value; Its First Real Check Measures 40.6
topSignals.whyItMatters: Paris's published 62.5 was never measured. A first evidence-based reading is 40.6 out of 100, at low confidence. The city's yearly homeless count earned credit. The October curfew was ordered by the national police, not the city.
topSignals.description:
Paris is ranked 30th among global cities with a published score of 62.5 out of 100, in the Established band (60 to 80). That number was never checked against evidence. A first full assessment measures 40.6, in the Functional band (40 to 60), with low confidence. The published score is unchanged, and the proposed change has not been applied.

This is a first measurement, not a measured decline in conduct. Most first measurements so far have come in below their starting value, so a calibration study is still open.

The credit side is homelessness. The City counted 3,858 people with no shelter on 22 January 2026, a record. It created 1,000 shelter places since 2023 and housed 253 evicted people in its own gyms in August 2026.

The 19 and 20 October 2026 curfew was ordered by the Paris police prefecture, a national government body. It is scored under France, not Paris.

Fifteen of the 40 sub-measures have no evidence and are scored at 2 out of 5. At the middle value of 3, Paris would read 50.0, still in the Functional band.

evidence.quote: 3 858 personnes rencontrées étaient sans solution d'hébergement durant la nuit du 22 janvier 2026.
evidence.claim: Paris's annual night count found 3,858 people with no shelter on 22 January 2026, a record and 10% more than the year before.

evidence.quote: 1000 places ont été créées depuis 2023 par la Ville de Paris
evidence.claim: Credited: the City created 1,000 shelter places since 2023, though the count still rose.

evidence.quote: au sein de gymnases de la Ville
evidence.claim: Credited: after a State eviction in August 2026 the City sheltered 253 people in its own gyms.

topSignals.title: UNC Chapel Hill Measures 28.1 Under One Rule and 41.3 Under Another
topSignals.whyItMatters: UNC settled 18 federal civil-rights probes without paying or admitting fault. A first reading is 28.1 out of 100. If missing evidence were scored 3 instead of 2, it would read 41.3, so the band depends on an unsettled rule.
topSignals.description:
The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC) is ranked 64th among 100 universities with a published score of 43.8 out of 100, in the Functional band (40 to 60). That number was never checked against evidence. A first full assessment measures 28.1, in the Developing band (20 to 40), with low confidence. The published score is unchanged, and the proposed change has not been applied.

This is a first measurement, not a measured decline in conduct. Most first measurements so far have come in below their starting value.

On 19 October 2026 UNC signed a voluntary agreement with the federal government that closed 18 Title VI civil-rights investigations. UNC paid nothing and admitted no wrongdoing. It must share complaints and report to the Justice Department every quarter. UNC had already closed its diversity offices and cut 61 positions by August 2026.

UNC is credited for the Carolina Covenant, which lets its lowest-income students graduate debt-free.

Twenty-one of the 40 sub-measures have no evidence. The assessment scores them at 2 out of 5. At 3, UNC would read 41.3, which stays in the Functional band. The band crossing exists only under the first rule.

evidence.quote: Within 90 days, share all complaints of alleged Title VI violations.
evidence.claim: The 19 October 2026 federal agreement requires UNC to hand over Title VI complaints and report to the Justice Department.

evidence.quote: 61 positions have been eliminated, and 27 others realigned as part of the changes.
evidence.claim: UNC had closed its diversity offices and cut 61 positions by August 2026.

evidence.quote: It's a way of bringing this means of repressing student protest and free speech onto this campus.
evidence.claim: A Jewish student, Zane Reed of TransparUNCy, said the deal could be used to repress protest.

topSignals.title: Portugal Measures 59.4 After Police Cleared Housing Camps in Lisbon and Porto
topSignals.whyItMatters: Portugal's published 60.6 sits 0.6 points above the Established line at 60. New evidence on police handling of housing protests puts the measured score at 59.4, just below it. Confidence is low and nothing is applied.
topSignals.description:
Portugal is ranked 39th among countries with a published score of 60.6 out of 100, in the Established band (60 to 80). A new assessment measures 59.4, in the Functional band (40 to 60), a difference of 1.2 points, at low confidence. The published score is unchanged, and the proposed change has not been applied.

Before dawn on 20 October 2026, national police cleared housing-protest camps in Lisbon and Porto and detained 55 people, according to Reuters. The police called the clearances calm and proportionate. Amnesty International Portugal asked on 15 October 2026 for an independent inquiry into an earlier Porto operation. Protesters said they were hit on the head.

On 30 September 2026 parliament backed a bill that speeds up evictions and ends rent controls on new leases.

Three sub-measures are now scored 3 instead of 4 out of 5: Validation, Priority for the Vulnerable, and Consistency Under Pressure. None of the adverse sources comes from a court, government watchdog or international body, so the crossing is filed at low confidence.

Lisbon's own pending 35.0 reading matched again. Its police seized 228 structures at the Rossio camp, and Mayor Carlos Moedas called the action proportionate.

evidence.quote: calm, proportionate and appropriate, with no police charge
evidence.claim: Portugal's national police described the 20 October 2026 camp clearances this way; 55 people were detained.

evidence.quote: As autoridades portuguesas devem garantir uma investigação independente, imparcial e eficaz da operação policial.
evidence.claim: Amnesty International Portugal asked on 15 October 2026 for an independent inquiry into the 12 October police operation in Porto.
On 30 September 2026 parliament backed a bill that speeds up evictions and ends rent controls on new leases.
Lisbon's police cleared the Rossio housing-protest camp on 20 October 2026, seizing 228 structures; Mayor Carlos Moedas called the action proportionate.

topSignals.title: France Measures 52.5 for the Second Time; the Riots Add No Top-Tier Source
topSignals.whyItMatters: France's riots from 17 October 2026 brought thousands of arrests and a minister's resignation offer. The measured score is 52.5 against a published 62.5, but no court or watchdog source backs a band crossing, so no proposal was filed.
topSignals.description:
France is ranked 28th among countries with a published score of 62.5 out of 100, in the Established band (60 to 80). That number is a shared starting value. A new assessment measures 52.5 for the second time, in the Functional band (40 to 60), at low confidence. The published score is unchanged. No proposal was filed.

The riots began on 17 October 2026. About 1,200 people were arrested that first evening, and about 2,400 later. Curfews followed, and a teenager lost a hand to a stun grenade. A police watchdog is examining about two dozen complaints of police violence. Interior Minister Nunez offered his resignation and President Emmanuel Macron rejected it.

The crossing is not filed for two reasons. No court, government watchdog or international body source was fetched; the sources are wire reports. And the starting value of 62.5 is shared with other unmeasured entities, so the gap reflects calibration as much as conduct.

The Paris curfew of 19 and 20 October 2026 was ordered by the national police prefecture and is scored under France. No sub-measure changed.

evidence.claim: Interior Minister Nunez offered his resignation after the riots that began on 17 October 2026; President Emmanuel Macron rejected it.
About 1,200 people were arrested on the first evening of the riots, and 150 police officers were injured.

topSignals.title: Storm Adam Matches Two Proposals Already on File for Spain and Valencia
topSignals.whyItMatters: Storm Adam killed at least four people in eastern Spain on 19 and 20 October 2026. Fresh readings of Spain (51.2) and Valencia (41.9) match proposals already on file. The published scores are 60.0 and 60.9 and nothing is applied.
topSignals.description:
Storm Adam brought up to about 700 litres of rain per square metre in 24 hours to eastern Spain on 19 and 20 October 2026. At least four people died, and about 800,000 residents were told to stay indoors under a regional order. National forces made more than 400 rescues.

Spain's published score is 60.0 out of 100. A new reading measures 51.2 for the third time, against 50.6 in the proposal filed on 26 August 2026. No sub-measure moved, and no duplicate proposal was written.

Valencia's published score is 60.9 out of 100. A new reading measures 41.9, identical to the proposal filed on 1 October 2026. The city of Valencia was outside the stay-indoors order for 145 municipalities. The deaths were in Oliva, Pego and Sagunto, so no municipal conduct was scored.

Both readings rest on earlier evidence. The storm adds context, not a new finding.

evidence.claim: Storm Adam killed at least four people in eastern Spain on 19 and 20 October 2026, with more than 400 rescues.
The regional government ordered residents of 145 municipalities to stay indoors on 19 October 2026; the city of Valencia was not on the list.

topSignals.title: Florida Carried Out Its 17th Execution of 2026; the Practice Is Already Scored
topSignals.whyItMatters: Florida executed James Robertson on 13 October 2026, two weeks after a failed execution in Tennessee. The practice is already in Florida's score. The reading is 37.5 out of 100 against a published 38.1.
topSignals.description:
Florida's published score is 38.1 out of 100, in the Developing band (20 to 40). The new reading is 37.5, within the 5-point threshold. The published score is confirmed and unchanged.

Florida executed James Robertson, 63, by lethal injection on 13 October 2026. It was the state's 17th execution of the year and its first since Tennessee's failed execution of Christa Pike. Governor Ron DeSantis paused the execution of Thompson, 74, who has a dementia claim, for now, according to EFE.

The repeated practice confirms the existing reading. Florida sits 1.9 points below the Functional line at 40.

evidence.claim: Florida executed James Robertson by lethal injection on 13 October 2026, its 17th execution of the year.
Florida's 17th execution of 2026 raised pressure against the death penalty; a separate execution, of Thompson, a 74-year-old with a dementia claim, was paused for now.

methodologyNotes.name: A First Measurement Is Not a Decline
methodologyNotes.description: Paris and UNC had never been checked against evidence. Their published scores of 62.5 and 43.8 were starting values. A first reading describes what the benchmark did not yet know, not what the institution did differently this week. Most first readings so far have come in below their starting value.

methodologyNotes.name: The Value Given to Missing Evidence Can Decide a Band
methodologyNotes.description: Where evidence is missing, these assessments score the gap at 2 out of 5. UNC has 21 such gaps and reads 28.1; at 3 it would read 41.3 and stay in the Functional band. Paris has 15 gaps and reads 40.6, or 50.0 at 3. The benchmark has not yet settled one convention.

methodologyNotes.name: We Score Who Caused the Harm
methodologyNotes.description: The Paris curfew was ordered by the national police prefecture, so it is scored under France. Lisbon's police cleared the Rossio camp itself, so that action counts under Lisbon. National police conduct in Porto and Lisbon counts under Portugal.

methodologyNotes.name: Source Quality Gates Band Crossings
methodologyNotes.description: A proposal that crosses a band line needs at least one strong source, such as a court, government or international body. None of tonight's three filings has one, so all three are filed at low confidence. France and Netflix cross the same lines on their measured values but were not filed.

methodologyNotes.name: No Evidence Found Means Not Surfaced
methodologyNotes.description: The search tool ignores OR and AND, and three search batches failed twice. An entity with no result was not surfaced; that is not a clean bill of health.

methodologyNotes.name: The Same Conduct Is Not Scored Twice
methodologyNotes.description: Florida's execution practice and the pending readings for Lisbon, Valencia and Spain were scored earlier. A new event of the same kind confirms the earlier reading but does not move it again.

dailyOpeningQuestion.text: UNC Chapel Hill measures 28.1 with missing evidence scored 2 and 41.3 scored 3; once the evidence-gap convention is settled, will it sit in the Developing band or the Functional band (40 to 60)?
dailyOpeningQuestion.tensionFraming: One university, two defensible rules for missing evidence, two different bands.
